minutes.headline: Committee voted an override amount of $715,000 to ask the town for, and approved a free-cash warrant article for network security.
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard the high school program of studies, the Student Opportunity Act plan, a quarterly budget report and a facilities update. It voted on a line-item transfer, a warrant article for network security and an override amount. Most of the night was FY25 budget discussion: the multiple budget versions, the 2.94% budget that must go to the finance committee, a Q&A, and the override figure.

attendees.role: vice chair of the finance committee

public_comment.topic: Chair asks for public comment at the start of the meeting; none heard in the room or on Zoom.
Resident asks whether cutting positions would change the health insurance line, and about the Chromebook and computer lease line.
Resident asks why the Turkey Hill fifth-grade band cut cannot be removed from the budget.
Resident asks how the level services minus Esser budget moved from about 8% to 6%, and where the extra reduction came from.
Parent and high school employee asks for a long-term plan for class sizes and course offerings so she can decide where to school her children.
Urges residents to attend the May 4th town meeting.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the January 24th regular session.
Approve the Lunenburg High School program of studies for 2024-25.
Approve the line-item transfer of $78,900 to cover line deficits.
Approve the language of the network security warrant article as drafted, for submission to annual town meeting.
Set the school override amount at $715,000.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported the town manager said not to count on additional funding, with a possible small amount from new growth.
The town manager had said an addition was possible pending new growth certification and a warrant article, then told the chair not to use it in planning.
The warrant total as of February 26th was stated.
The principal said AP Statistics would add no cost because textbooks were already bought.
The line is over by roughly the cost of an added out-of-district placement. It will be covered with prior-year circuit breaker money.
Funds were moved from various lines to offset deficits.
The article would transfer free cash to pay for the network security upgrade, and the amount was read as a garbled figure.

budget_items.topic: High school dishwasher booster tank repair
budget_items.what_was_said: The repair of the booster tank cost about this amount.
Replacing the pump motor and starter was a significant cost, and a further hydraulic leak quote is being sought.
A circulation pump rebuild and actuator replacement were reported.
Sensor replacement and one controller replacement were reported, plus a service technician day rate.
The preferred contractor's cost came in just under the budget, funded through OPA funds.

budget_items.topic: Network upgrade funds removed to reach 2.94%
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent removed funds from the computer lease and maintenance line to bring the 3.02% budget down to 2.94%.
The budget with actual position cuts came to a stated dollar total, 6.04% over the current year.
A member noted the side-by-side sheet carries a different dollar total than the new slide.
The line includes Chromebook replacement, staff device replacement and security upgrades, with part of the earmark removed.
Level services was stated unchanged, and the level services minus Esser total was repeated.
A figure for the gap above the town manager's budget was worked out aloud, with a possible $230,000 more if it comes through.
A member said the retired-debt savings are tied to excludable debt and not discretionary money.
The committee settled on rounding the gap up to a round override figure, which was moved and voted.
A member estimated the cost of replacing the comfort dog, all in with training.

budget_items.topic: Council on Aging and library staffing (finance committee report)
budget_items.what_was_said: A member reported finance committee discussion of meal site manager hours and library hours.

transfers.description: Various line items moved to offset deficits in the lines listed on the transfer form
Warrant article to transfer from free cash for the network security upgrade

decisions.decision: The chair and superintendent will not use the $230,000 in budget planning; it will not appear.
The committee agreed the superintendent will present the 2.94% budget to the finance committee, since that is what the town manager's omnibus budget requires.
The chair will work out the override wording with the select board; the intended language is to support the education of Lunenburg students.
The legal notice for the March 20th budget hearing will use the level services minus Esser figure as a placeholder.
The finance director position was agreed not to be cut, and the superintendent was told she can post it.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to set the school override amount, the figure it will ask the town to approve.
The committee agreed the superintendent will present the budget that fits the town manager's omnibus budget to the finance committee.
The committee voted 5-0 to approve the network security warrant article, which transfers free cash, for annual town meeting.
The committee voted 5-0 on a line-item transfer to cover line deficits, and 5-0 to approve the high school program of studies for 2024-25.
The legal notice for the March 20th budget hearing will use the level services minus Esser figure as a placeholder.

why_it_matters: The override amount is the figure residents are likely to be asked to vote on, and an override raises property tax bills above the levy cap if approved.
The network security article draws on free cash, so it is another item on the annual town meeting warrant that residents will vote on.
watch_next: The March 20th budget hearing, whose legal notice will carry a placeholder figure.
The May 4th town meeting, which a speaker urged residents to attend.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all four votes (program of studies, line item transfers, network security warrant article, $715,000 override) and their unanimous outcomes; the differences are mostly caption-garbled figures and names. The one thing to check is that our minutes carry several decisions and facilities figures the official minutes omit, plus an unresolved 6.04% vs 6.02% level services percentage.
